title: ULPF normalized event (OCSF JSON + _lineage envelope)
description: The runtime's output record for one event: an OCSF event object (class_uid and the attributes the pack maps, nested as OCSF objects) plus the mandatory _lineage block (architecture §4.1) and the unmapped vendor extensions. OCSF attributes themselves are validated against the pinned class table by the pack, not enumerated here; this contract fixes the envelope so the learning plane's differential test (P3) can compare outputs field for field. Frozen at P2 exit.

category_uid.description: 1.1.0. Derived from the class via the pinned table.

type_uid.description: 1.1.0. class_uid * 100 + activity_id (0 when activity_id is absent).

severity_id.description: 1.1.0. Pack-declared (constant or mapped) with provenance — a judgement, never derived.

metadata.description: 1.1.0. OCSF metadata: version and product from the pack.

unmapped.description: Vendor extensions carried under their pack-declared names; values are the decoded span values.

schema_version.description: 1.1.0 (P3 boundary) is additive over 1.0.0; 1.2.0 (P5) adds the optional envelope record; 1.3.0 (P7) adds the relay chain (recursive unwrap), the CEF application envelope, the batch record of a de-batched element, and the udp_datagram framing method; 1.4.0 adds the LEEF application envelope (kind leef: the header is carried in version, device_vendor, device_product, device_version, signature_id = the LEEF event id, and leef_delimiter for LEEF 2.0; the payload is the attribute list); every bump is additive and earlier documents remain valid.

framing.description: Structured framing record: reconstruction is raw_prefix + raw + raw_suffix (base64).

relay_chain.description: 1.3.0 (P7). Every envelope removed by recursive unwrap, outermost first, when there was more than one: up to two syslog envelopes (a relay re-wrapping a device header) plus one CEF application envelope. The last entry equals envelope. Absent when at most one envelope was removed.

batch.description: 1.3.0 (P7). Present when the event is one element of a de-batched JSON array: the sha256 of the whole received batch, this element's index and the batch size. The element's own raw bytes are hashed in raw_hash; the batch is reconstructible from its elements' framing records.

routing_signature.description: The L1–L4 signature key the event matched, as computed by the router.

normalization_version.description: Corrections emit a new version with derived_from (invariant 8, P8); v1 is never rewritten.

absent.description: Mapped mandatory attributes that have no value in this event, with the cause. Mandatory is a mapping obligation, not a per-event presence requirement: the event is usable; the absence is a recorded fact. 'structural' = the source carried no span for the field; 'uncoercible' = a span exists but its value failed coercion (e.g. a vendor null marker such as Squid's '-'). Omitted when empty.

cause.description: declared_null (1.1.0): the source carried a pack-declared null marker for the field.

envelope.description: 1.2.0 (P5). The transport envelope unwrapped before routing. The raw evidence record holds the complete received bytes; offset/length above address them. payload_offset/payload_length locate, within those bytes, the payload the parser saw; span offsets in the parser's span map are relative to the payload. Header fields are carried verbatim as the envelope stated them — the envelope's own timestamp is the relay's clock unless a pack says otherwise (temporal_role). 1.3.0 (P7): when a relay chain was unwrapped this is the INNERMOST envelope (the device's own header, the one routing anchors and envelope-sourced mappings read) and relay_chain holds every envelope removed, outermost first; level is the envelope's position in that chain (1 = outermost). kind cef is the ArcSight CEF application header, unwrapped after the transport envelopes; its seven header fields are carried in device_vendor … cef_severity and the payload is the extension.

version.description: RFC 5424 VERSION (1 or more) or the CEF version (0 for CEF:0).

leef_delimiter.description: 1.4.0, kind leef, LEEF 2.0 only: the attribute delimiter the header declares, as written (a character or 0xHH / xHH).
